def-wishart-law:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $p,m\ge1$ be integers and let $\Sigma$ be a real symmetric positive-semidefinite $p\times p$ matrix, in the sense of [[def-multivariate-normal-law]]. Give $\mathrm{Sym}_p$, the space of real symmetric $p\times p$ matrices, its Euclidean Borel sigma-algebra by identifying a matrix with its upper-triangular entries. The finite product measure $N_p(0,\Sigma)^{\otimes m}$ exists because each factor is a probability measure and hence sigma-finite. Define the **Wishart law** $W_p(\Sigma,m)$ as the pushforward of this product measure by the continuous map $(z_1,\ldots,z_m)\mapsto\sum_{j=1}^m z_jz_j^T$. Equivalently, it is the law of $\sum_{j=1}^m Z_jZ_j^T$ for independent $Z_j\sim N_p(0,\Sigma)$.

Here $\Sigma$ is the scale matrix and the positive integer $m$ is the degrees of freedom. This definition allows a singular Wishart law when $m<p$ or $\Sigma$ is singular; no Lebesgue density is included in the convention. The usual nonsingular density when $m\ge p$ is not needed below.
lem-standard-normal-matrix-has-full-row-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $1\le p\le m$ and let $G=[G_1|\cdots|G_m]$ be a $p\times m$ matrix whose columns are independent $N_p(0,I_p)$ random vectors. Then the first $p$ columns are linearly independent almost surely. Consequently $GG^T$ is positive definite almost surely.
def-multivariate-normal-sample-model-and:
## Definition

Assume AC. Fix integers $n\ge2$ and $p\ge1$. Let $\mathcal S_{++}^p$ be the set of real symmetric $p\times p$ matrices $\Sigma$ such that $v^T\Sigma v>0$ for every nonzero $v\in\mathbb R^p$. The iid multivariate-normal sampling experiment has data space $\mathcal X=(\mathbb R^p)^n$ with sigma-algebra $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^p)^{\otimes n}$, parameter set $\Theta=\mathbb R^p\times\mathcal S_{++}^p$, and sampling law $P_{\mu,\Sigma}=N_p(\mu,\Sigma)^{\otimes n}$. The finite product is a probability measure by [[def-probability-measure]] and [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]]. The coordinate projection $X_i$ is the complete vector observation for sampling unit $i$; its $p$ coordinates need not be independent.

For $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathcal X$, define
$$\bar x=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i,\qquad R(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i-\bar x)(x_i-\bar x)^T,\qquad S(x)=\frac{R(x)}{n-1},\qquad M(x)=\frac{R(x)}n.$$
The functions $x\mapsto\bar x$, $S(x)$, and $M(x)$ are continuous, hence Borel measurable under AC and [[lem-ac-supplies-sequential-choices-for-probability-constructions]]; they are statistics in the experiment by [[def-statistic-and-estimator]]. Here $S$ uses the $n-1$ covariance denominator, while $M$ is the $n$-denominator covariance candidate whose maximum-likelihood property is proved separately below.

This item instantiates the mathematical portion of the scientific model contract ([[def-scientific-statistical-model-contract]]) as follows. One sampling and analysis unit is one complete observed vector $X_i$; index $i$ identifies the sampling unit and coordinate $a$ identifies a component within that vector. For fixed parameter label $\theta=(\mu,\Sigma)$, $\mu$ and $\Sigma$ are fixed, every $X_i$ is random, every component of each $X_i$ is observed, and there are no latent quantities, predictors, treatments, or randomization. The target population for this reference experiment is the abstract law $N_p(\mu,\Sigma)$ of a vector-valued sampling unit, and the target parameter is $\theta$ itself; no separate scientific estimand or physical setting is asserted. The observation map records the complete vector tuple unchanged, and inference uses the joint product law, with no conditioning convention beyond that law. No topological support or empirical adequacy claim is needed; this is a mathematical reference model, not an assertion that observed scientific data follow it.
lem-standard-wishart-independent-normal-:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $m\ge p\ge1$, let $W\sim W_p(I_p,m)$, and let $Z\sim N_p(0,I_p)$ be independent of $W$. Then $W$ is positive definite almost surely and
$$\frac{m-p+1}{p}Z^TW^{-1}Z\sim F_{p,m-p+1}.$$
thm-multivariate-normal-sample-mean-scat:
## Statement

Assume AC and the sample model in [[def-multivariate-normal-sample-model-and-statistics]], with $n\ge2$, $p\ge1$, and $\Sigma\succ0$. Then
$$\sqrt n(\bar X-\mu)\sim N_p(0,\Sigma),\qquad \bar X\perp S,\qquad (n-1)S\sim W_p(\Sigma,n-1).$$
If $n>p$, then $S$ is positive definite almost surely. The Wishart scale is $\Sigma$ and its degrees of freedom are $n-1$.
thm-covariance-likelihood-ratio-asymptot:
## Statement

Assume AC, fix $p\ge1$, and use the iid multivariate-normal sample model with $n>p$. Test $H_0:\Sigma=\Sigma_0$ against unrestricted $\Sigma\in\mathcal S_{++}^p$, with $\mu\in\mathbb R^p$ unrestricted under both hypotheses and fixed $\Sigma_0\succ0$. Let $M=R/n$ be the full-model Gaussian covariance MLE, and let $\Lambda_n$ be the null-over-full maximized likelihood ratio formed from the explicit Lebesgue Gaussian density. Almost surely,
$$-2\log\Lambda_n=n\left[\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_0^{-1}M)-\log\det(\Sigma_0^{-1/2}M\Sigma_0^{-1/2})-p\right].$$
With $p$ fixed and the null true, $-2\log\Lambda_n\Rightarrow\chi^2_{p(p+1)/2}$ as $n\to\infty$. The covariance null is interior in $\mathcal S_{++}^p$. This calibration is asymptotic; no finite-sample chi-square law is asserted.
thm-hotelling-t2-exact-f-distribution:
## Statement

Assume AC, $n>p\ge1$, and the iid multivariate-normal sample model with covariance $\Sigma\succ0$. For $\mu_0\in\mathbb R^p$, define $T^2=n(\bar X-\mu_0)^TS^{-1}(\bar X-\mu_0)$ when $S\succ0$, and set $T^2=0$ otherwise. Under $H_0:\mu=\mu_0$,
$$\frac{n-p}{p(n-1)}T^2\sim F_{p,n-p}.$$
The zero extension does not change the law because $S\succ0$ almost surely when $n>p$.
thm-wishart-trace-statistic-is-chi-squar:
## Statement

Assume AC, $p\ge1$, $n\ge2$, and the iid multivariate-normal sample model. Under $H_0:\Sigma=\Sigma_0$ for a specified $\Sigma_0\succ0$, the distinct statistic
$$\operatorname{tr}\{\Sigma_0^{-1}(n-1)S\}$$
has the exact law $\chi^2_{p(n-1)}$, even when $n\le p$ and $S$ is singular. This is the Wishart trace statistic, not the covariance likelihood-ratio statistic.
cor-exact-hotelling-one-sample-test:
## Statement

Assume AC, $n>p\ge1$, and the one-sample multivariate-normal model with covariance $\Sigma\succ0$. For a specified $\mu_0\in\mathbb R^p$ and $0<\alpha<1$, reject $H_0:\mu=\mu_0$ when
$$\frac{n-p}{p(n-1)}T^2>F_{p,n-p}^{-1}(1-\alpha),$$
where $T^2$ is the statistic in [[thm-hotelling-t2-exact-f-distribution]]. Against $H_1:\mu\ne\mu_0$, this test has size exactly $\alpha$ over all null covariances $\Sigma\succ0$.
